newsitem.title: USA: Digital cuts prices on some computers.
newsitem.headline: Digital cuts prices on some computers.

text.p: Computer maker Digital Equipment Corp. Thursday announced price cuts of up to 47 percent in high-end workstations and network computers running on its Alpha microprocessor and costing tens or hundreds of thousands of dollars.
The cuts are part of an effort to better compete with lower-priced but slower systems from Hewlett-Packard Co., Silicon Graphics Inc. and Sun Microsystems Inc., a Digital spokesman said.
They also reflect volume manufacturing and cheaper memory for its AlphaServer line of servers, the computers that run networks, the Maynard, Mass.-based company said.
The main customers for the computers are engineers and designers at businesses such as aircraft manufacturers and automakers.
The AlphaServer price cuts are effective worldwide, while the reductions on prices for Digital's AlphaStations apply in Europe and the United States, the company said.

Among the cuts, the price of Digital's midrange AlphaServer 4000 5/300 system with 512 megabytes of random access memory, or RAM, will drop 47 percent to $31,500. Digital's AlphaServer 8200 5/440 with two gigabytes of memory falls 20 percent to $224,400.

Digital's AlphaStation 600/333 with 128 megabytes of memory was cut 42 percent to $24,995 and its AlphaStation 500/500, which it calls the world's fastest desktop workstation, with 128 megabytes of memory, drops 20 percent to $39,995.
Digital also said it introduced new server configurations that provide as much as four times the memory of current systems at little or no extra cost.
